title: Unchecked fee option still increases the donation total
evidence: At initial load, the fee checkbox is unchecked. Selecting $100 shows Donate $102.90. Checking and then unchecking the option changes the button to Donate $100. Source initializes st.fee from the campaign but never initializes the checkbox to that value.
recommendation: Default optional fee coverage to off, synchronize displayed checkbox and application state, and calculate the displayed amount from the same choice sent to checkout.
acceptance: Fresh load: unchecked + $100 shows $100. Checked shows the disclosed fee. Unchecked returns to $100. Verify checkout amount and receipt in an approved test flow.

title: Monthly giving promise has no monthly selection
evidence: The settled live giving form exposes amount buttons and a donation button, with no frequency control. The homepage says Give monthly; page metadata and contact copy also promise monthly gifts.
recommendation: Enable and verify recurring giving in the campaign and UI, or align the public messaging with the actual supported flow until it is ready.
acceptance: A visitor following Give monthly can explicitly choose and review a monthly gift before checkout; frequency remains visible through the approved test flow.

title: Donation presets differ from the agreed selection
evidence: Live presets are $25, $50, $100, $250 and Custom. The project direction calls for $50, $100, $250, $500 and Other.
recommendation: Align the campaign presets with the agreed donation options and use one label for the custom amount.
acceptance: Fresh live form displays the agreed amounts and a working custom-amount control.

title: Placeholder clinician identities are public
evidence: Clinical Director, SLP, PT and counselor profiles show Sample Name alongside credentials and detailed biographies; illustrated/placeholder portraits are visible.
recommendation: Replace each with verified, approved clinician information and authorized portraits. Suppress unfilled profiles rather than publishing sample identities.
acceptance: No sample identities or unverified credentials remain. Every published profile has an accountable content owner.

title: Callback form prompt contradicts its privacy instruction
evidence: The page says callback details only and asks visitors not to include diagnoses or treatment information. Its free-text label asks them to describe their child and what they are looking for.
recommendation: Use a narrowly scoped contact or scheduling prompt, or remove the field. Put concise guidance beside the field; collect clinical information through the approved intake process.
acceptance: Field labels, help text, privacy copy and confirmation consistently request callback logistics without inviting clinical details.

title: Newsletter subscription reuses the contact form
evidence: The Updates from Faith Reins area renders Your name*, Email*, Phone and Message*, with a Subscribe button. Message is required for a newsletter signup.
recommendation: Use a dedicated subscription form with email, optional name and appropriate subscription confirmation.
acceptance: A visitor can subscribe without writing a message; the resulting confirmation describes subscription rather than a general inquiry.

title: Insurance statements disagree between pages
evidence: Payment & Insurance says the practice is working to accept major commercial insurance plans. The FAQ says it works with major commercial insurance plans.
recommendation: Have operations confirm current payer participation and use the same qualified statement in every location.
acceptance: FAQ, service pages, intake copy and payment page agree with the current verified coverage information.

title: Hero secondary action changes its visual role by device
evidence: Our therapies is a small uppercase underlined text link beside a filled callback button. The mobile CSS turns .hero__sec into a padded outlined control. Shop editorial links use a separate sentence-case style and down arrow.
recommendation: Define primary action, secondary action and editorial text-link roles. Apply the chosen secondary CTA consistently; keep ordinary text links and disclosure controls distinct.
acceptance: A documented role/state matrix covers light/dark surfaces, desktop/tablet/mobile, hover, focus and disabled states; all uses match it.

title: Callback terminology drifts to appointment and booking language
evidence: Contact still includes Book online and Request an appointment. Payment and FAQ CTAs also say Request an appointment. These destinations lead to the callback page.
recommendation: Use Request a callback for this funnel and explain that scheduling follows the conversation. Keep established URLs unless a separately planned redirect is needed.
acceptance: Every visible CTA and related instruction accurately describes the destination and expected outcome.

title: Layers remains in product taxonomy
evidence: Product recommendation cards still label vest/quarter-zip products Layers, while category navigation uses Outerwear.
recommendation: Use Outerwear consistently in catalog data, cards, filters and recommendations.
acceptance: No customer-facing Layers taxonomy remains where Outerwear is intended.

title: EAL inherits clinical-payment framing
evidence: EAL is described as a nonclinical ground-based program, but its hero and closing CTA both foreground Payment & insurance and the closing copy mentions coverage. It reuses clinical-template wording about individualized plans.
recommendation: Give EAL its own program fit, participation, safety and payment explanation; describe any funding arrangements accurately and retain the explicit nonclinical distinction.
acceptance: The page clearly explains EAL participation and the correct next step without implying clinical insurance coverage.

title: Impact page provides principles without evidence of impact
evidence: The page lists funding areas and stewardship principles, but offers no dated results, reporting period, financial summary, report download or measurable outcomes.
recommendation: Publish verified dated results and reporting links when available. Until then, clearly describe stewardship commitments and provide a route for donor questions.
acceptance: Impact claims have a period, source and owner; the page delivers evidence appropriate to its promise.

title: Partner/sponsor area exposes placeholder graphics
evidence: The sponsor section contains tier placeholder graphics and empty-looking sponsor positions rather than a complete set of identified current partners.
recommendation: Publish only confirmed sponsor identities with permission; hide empty tiers or present a clearly labeled sponsorship opportunity separately.
acceptance: Every displayed sponsor is identifiable and approved; no placeholder logo or empty sponsor slot is presented as a current supporter.

title: Legacy men route sends conflicting canonical signals
evidence: The HTTP response contains canonicals for both /shop/men.html and /shop/mens.html. It returns 200, is noindex, appears in the sitemap and moves to /shop/men.html through page-level redirect behavior.
recommendation: Use one server-level permanent redirect to the selected canonical route and remove the legacy URL from the XML sitemap.
acceptance: One canonical destination; a direct permanent HTTP redirect; no competing canonical or legacy sitemap entry.

title: Published XML sitemap includes unsuitable and broken entries
evidence: The page sitemap includes seven noindex URLs (six account routes and /shop/mens.html), /news/post.html, and giving/order thank-you pages. A separate pricing-plan sitemap advertises /pricing-plans/plans-pricing, which returns HTTP 404.
recommendation: Reconcile the hosting-generated sitemap with canonical indexable pages. Exclude account, redirect, parameterized template and confirmation URLs; remove the broken pricing-plan entry.
acceptance: Every listed URL resolves successfully to an intended canonical indexable page; source exclusions are verified in the published sitemap.

title: Hosting output duplicates canonical and social-title metadata
evidence: All 94 registered-page responses contain two canonical elements and two og:title elements. The values generally agree, but the legacy men route conflicts (FR-14). The source layout and published hosting output need one SEO owner.
recommendation: Resolve duplicate metadata at the source/hosting boundary rather than deleting valid SEO arbitrarily.
acceptance: Exactly one canonical and one intended social title are emitted per canonical page, with page-appropriate social previews.

title: Most product detail guides remain reference placeholders
evidence: There are 21 detailed showcase pages. Only two include any garment measurement table; those tables apply to specific proposed variants. The other pages explicitly defer measurements, capacity, composition or care details.
recommendation: Retain honest unavailable/reference language now. Before selling, finish the Printful supplier mapping and variant-specific dimensions, materials and care details; avoid a measurement-guide label that promises a table when none exists.
acceptance: Each sellable variant has verified supplier details, and guide labels accurately describe available information.

title: Legacy product pages recommend unrelated products
evidence: Unavailable legacy destinations retain their old title but often show the same four polo recommendations. Beanie, keychain and sticker visitors are sent to polo choices.
recommendation: Use relevant category alternatives and a clear current-category link; decide which legacy pages should remain indexable versus redirect to a useful equivalent.
acceptance: Every retained legacy route has a clear purpose and relevant next destination; unavailable items remain clearly labeled.

title: Required fields and errors lack programmatic associations
evidence: The five visually required callback fields have neither required nor aria-required. Controls have no aria-describedby. Empty submission creates error alerts and focuses the first field, but the renderer does not associate the error with that field or set aria-invalid. V7 component guidance explicitly calls for help/error IDs and programmatic error association.
recommendation: Add required semantics, stable help/error IDs, aria-describedby and error-state attributes to the shared renderer. Preserve the working first-error focus behavior.
acceptance: Assistive technology can identify required fields and read the relevant help/error text on focus; test empty and invalid input states.

title: Recurring-gift management copy promises different capabilities
evidence: The donation policy says a donor can modify or cancel a recurring gift by logging in. The recurring account page describes recorded payments and contacting the team about changes; account help likewise routes changes to staff.
recommendation: Confirm the actual supported management flow and align policy, account copy and giving confirmations. Verify any self-service change/cancel function with an approved test account.
acceptance: A donor receives one accurate set of instructions; authenticated management behavior is tested before a self-service promise is published.

title: Unknown routes show a generic hosting error experience
evidence: A deliberately nonexistent URL returns HTTP 404 with the hosting platform's generic Page Not Found document rather than the Faith Reins shell. /404.html itself returns 200. A custom source error page alone does not prove hosting is using it.
recommendation: Wire the branded error experience into production routing, including useful home, services and contact paths while preserving the correct error status.
acceptance: An unknown path returns 404 and gives visitors a recognizable, navigable Faith Reins recovery page.

title: News index and seasonal next steps are stale or weakly ordered
evidence: The index lists August, September and October stories in ascending date order. The summer recap still says fall registration opens in September, although the audit is in October. Hiring/age-range statements need alignment with current pages and the established pediatric wording.
recommendation: Use an intentional news sort, update or date-limit seasonal calls to action, and revalidate recruitment and audience statements.
acceptance: Newest/current updates are easy to identify; expired next-step copy is archived or updated.

title: Substantiate clinical, testimonial and program claims
evidence: Published copy includes anonymous clinical-progress testimonials, detailed clinician biographies, a twelve-participant/eight-week summer program narrative, and clinical-evidence language. This audit cannot verify their truth or publication permissions.
recommendation: Maintain an approval register identifying the factual source, owner, consent where applicable and review date. Remove or replace unsupported claims; do not invent replacement outcomes.
acceptance: Each claim and testimonial has documented substantiation and approval; scope and qualifications match current operations.

title: Verify the shared address, ZIP and map coordinates
evidence: The footer and organization schema publish Camden, AR 72711; schema also contains latitude 33.5843 and longitude -92.8343. These need verification against the actual facility/mailing address and entrance. No replacement ZIP or coordinate is assumed here.
recommendation: Confirm address and map destination with operations, then use one approved record in footer, contact, directions, schema and external listings.
acceptance: All location representations agree with the verified facility record; directions lead to the correct entrance.

title: Align public policies with current operations
evidence: Policies make specific promises about pre-intake information, recurring-gift management, accepted payment methods, shipping/returns, response periods, consent and mounted-activity rules. Program pages describe ground-based EAL. This is a content/operations verification request, not a legal compliance conclusion.
recommendation: Have accountable clinical, operational and policy reviewers confirm the actual practices; reconcile policy language with site functionality and program scope.
acceptance: Each policy has an owner, approved current text and review date; public instructions match the available services and systems.

title: Reproduce the supplied compact-screen and clipped-menu examples
evidence: The supplied compact shop screenshot shows a heading crowded beneath the header; another screenshot shows a clipped menu edge. At the available 1363px desktop viewport, all six menu panels fit within the viewport. The supplied captures do not establish exact width, scroll position or current build.
recommendation: Reproduce at 320/390/430, 768/1024, 1280/1440 and either side of 767/1023/1279px breakpoints; test scroll/anchor states, image crops, wrapping, focus and touch behavior.
acceptance: Record exact device/viewport/browser and before/after evidence. Do not close from desktop or CSS inspection alone.
